notes:
Summary: Enterprise maritime analytics provider evaluating Redwood Dedicated for real-time on-bridge assistance, log embeddings for search, and reranking for route suggestions. Primary driver is deterministic throughput during port-traffic spikes and strict latency SLOs for captain-facing tooling.

Workload profile (customer-supplied estimates / traces):
- Baseline steady-state QPS: 20–35 requests/sec (typical daytime operations).
- Average per-request tokens: 120 tokens input + 280 tokens output (templated explanations + route contexts) => ~400 tokens/req.
- Calculated steady-state token/sec: 20 * 400 = 8,000 tps (lower bound) to 35 * 400 = 14,000 tps (upper bound).
- Peak / burst scenario (harbor approach & emergency mode): short bursts up to 110–130 QPS observed in traces. Peak token/sec ~ 130 * 400 = 52,000 tps.
- Traffic shape: diurnal with scheduled surges (arrival windows), 10–20s tail bursts from telemetry fan-in.

Latency & SLO targets:
- Captain UI (interactive chat): p50 < 100ms, p95 < 250ms (streaming-friendly).
- Backend reranking endpoints: p50 < 80ms, p95 < 220ms.
- Throughput guarantee desired: consistent sustained throughput with headroom for 2x expected steady-state during business hours; firm burst capacity for short peaks.

Model & routing preferences:
- Primary model candidate: 70B-class open model (quantized 4-bit) for accuracy on maritime instructions; fallback smaller 13B variant for heavy bursts to preserve latency.
- Prefer run-time routing by policy: latency-first for captain UI, cost-first for batch embedding jobs.

GPU/reserved capacity planning (initial sizing thoughts from SE session):
- Observed token/sec translated to approximate GPU requirements (rough heuristic): H100-class node ~ 1.6k–2.4k tokens/sec for gen workload on 70B quantized depending on batch and sequence length.
- Steady-state (8k–14k tps) => estimate 6–9 H100 nodes for baseline sustained throughput.
- Headroom for 2x steady-state & short peak handling to 52k tps => planning burst pool / autoscale to 18–24 H100 nodes or allow rapid fallback to 13B model (reduces token cost by ~3–4x).
- Customer prefers reserved pool for predictable costs but wants burst autoscaling to dedicated spare capacity (policy + pre-warm).
- Prefers Dedicated with VPC (private control plane) + KMS for keys and 2-year audit log retention.

SLA negotiation points flagged:
- Target uptime: 99.95% SLA (enterprise).
- Remedies: financial credits tied to sustained under-provisioning, not single degraded request.
- Latency SLOs: define p95 latency windows and rollback policy if SLOs are missed; want automatic fallback to 13B variant with no request loss.
- Support: 24/7 priority escalation channel, 4h P1 response and 24h resolution targets for infra-impacting incidents.

Operational needs & data governance:
- Data residency: primary US East, secondary EU zone for certain clients (must support per-customer region pinning).
- Audit: immutable audit logs, 2-year retention, exportable for compliance.
- Networking: allow egress lock-down, static peering IPs, and explicit port list for certification.

Next steps (short-term):
- Schedule 2-hour dedicated capacity sizing workshop (SE-led) to run through: 7-day traffic trace walkthrough, tokenization verification, model SAR (sequence attenuation) testing, and microbenchmarking on a 70B quantized profile. SE to bring bench numbers and cost scenarios.
- Customer to confirm NDA + provide sanitized traces by 2026-03-15.
- AE and Legal to finalize MSA draft for Dedicated pilot (30–60 day trial).

Open questions / blockers:
- Final model family choice — if customer requires LLM fine-tune, embedding dims and retraining cadence will change sizing.
- Procurement timeline for reserved capacity (capex vs opex).
- Security team requires penetration test window — scheduling TBD.

Notes from call (quotes / paraphrases):
- "We need predictable behavior during the 20 minutes around port approach — a dropped response there is costly." — Head of Engineering.
- "If Redwood can guarantee steady throughput and provide a fallback model with automatic routing, we can commit to a 12-month reserved pool."
